narrative:
The model estimates an 85% chance that you will leave your job. Because promotion decisions here use that retention risk, this high likelihood is the reason you are being denied a promotion at this time.

The strongest signal is your overall work experience of 6–10 years. Among employees predicted to stay, most have only 1–5 years, so your longer career record suggests greater mobility. Second, your 1–5 years in the current organization also pushes toward leaving; although this tenure is common among stayers, combined with your total experience it suggests you may be at a career transition point. Third, having other job opportunities is a meaningful push toward leaving, since only about one in four employees predicted to stay report such opportunities.

Other warning signs include low satisfaction with pay, recognition, environment and the job overall, no bonus or medical insurance, low emotional commitment, feeling the deserved promotion was not received, job instability, overtime, and difficult work-life balance.

The organization should discuss a clear career path, recognition, pay and benefits, workload, and concrete promotion criteria with you. You should clarify what would keep you, seek feedback and development, and weigh your outside options carefully. Because the denial rests on predicted exit, a retention plan and promotion-readiness review should come next.
